title: Coherent effects in quantum transport models and their classical counterparts
authors: N. S. Maslova, V. N. Mantsevich, I. M. Sokolov, P. I. Arseyev
abstract: We analyze the transport properties of quasiparticles locally excited at an initial time moment in several exactly solvable quantum models. It is revealed that, in the investigated quantum systems, the time-dependent probability distribution function (PDF) exhibits behavior similar to that of classical continuous-time random walk (CTRW) models, such as Lévy walks or diffusing diffusivity.
summary: The paper investigates quasiparticle transport in various quantum chain models, demonstrating that the time evolution of the probability distribution function mimics classical random walk behaviors. By analyzing phonon-assisted hopping and disordered chains, the authors establish a direct quantum analogue to anomalous diffusion processes, particularly those exhibiting ballistic or U-shaped spreading.
main_problem: The study analyzes how quasiparticle transport properties behave in quantum systems, specifically comparing coherent quantum dynamics to classical stochastic models like Lévy walks.
main_result: Quantum probability distributions exhibit behavior analogous to classical Continuous-Time Random Walk (CTRW) models, showing ballistic spreading or U-shaped profiles due to underlying coherence mechanisms.
method: The analysis involves solving time evolution equations for the probability distribution function (PDF) using tight-binding Hamiltonians and applying advanced mathematical techniques like integral transforms and saddle-point approximations.
model_or_system: The models include simple tight-binding chains, heterogeneous ensembles of chains with random hopping amplitudes, and phonon-assisted hopping mechanisms in 2D semiconductor systems (like TMDs).
key_observables: Time-dependent probability distribution function (PDF) $P_j(t)$, mean squared displacement $\langle x^2 angle$, and the shape transition of the PDF (bimodal to monomodal).
important_parameters: Hopping amplitude ($T$), phonon coupling strength ($\omega_{ct}$), disorder parameters ($\mu, \sigma$), and time $t$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations such as the continuum limit, saddle-point approximation for integrals, and assuming specific forms for random phases or hopping amplitudes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the quasi-particle PDF ($P_j$) showing transitions from bimodal to monomodal shapes in heterogeneous ensembles, and demonstrate U-shaped/ballistic profiles in phonon-assisted hopping models.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes transport using several quantum models: simple tight-binding, heterogeneous ensembles (varying disorder), random time-dependent hopping, and finally the detailed analysis of phonon-assisted hopping mechanisms.
why_interesting: This work bridges coherent quantum dynamics with classical anomalous diffusion processes, providing a microscopic quantum origin for phenomena like Lévy walks observed in condensed matter systems.
